raw_response:
I've been farming this land for over 40 years. My father farmed it before me. In Quzhou, you grow wheat in winter and corn in summer — that's just what you do here. The land is flat, the soil is okay, and we have the well. I have about 12 mu total.

Wheat goes in around the 10th of October. I'll use Jimai 22 — my neighbor got good results last year and the seed station sells it. For corn I use the hybrid, Xianyu 335, same as I've used for years. I trust it.

Water is the big problem. Electricity for the pump is expensive and the water table keeps dropping. I'll irrigate wheat three times — once before winter sets in, once in jointing, once at heading. Corn I'll water twice — at planting and if it gets dry at silking. Rain usually helps in July.

Fertilizer: I buy the compound bag (15-15-15) and then add urea on top during the season. Probably more than the technicians say I should, but I'd rather not lose the crop.

I'll spray herbicide on the wheat in spring and do one fungicide spray if I see any rust. Corn gets a herbicide pass after planting, and I watch for armyworm.

I use rotary tillage before wheat — I've never tried no-till, I don't trust it.
